analysis.title: GS Armbrust - What Matters Today: Heavy Shorting + Record Tech Selling = Sharp Net Leverage Reduction, SpaceX Blowout Earnings
key_insights: A hotter-than-expected US CPI print and renewed doubts over the payoff from heavy AI capex sparked a sharp unwind in semis and AI infrastructure names in October. The unwind began in Asian memory stocks.
Hedge funds have heavily net sold global equities month to date. Short sales far outpaced long buys, at roughly 5 to 1.

Hedge fund long leverage sits in the 73rd percentile vs. the past year (94th percentile over 5 years). Short leverage has risen sharply and is approaching 5-year highs in the 99th percentile, which GS flags as a possible short squeeze risk.

Nearly all major regions except Europe are net sold in October, led by North America and EM Asia. Within Asia, Taiwan, Japan and Korea are the most notionally net sold markets, while Australia and Hong Kong are the most net bought.
Net allocation to Korea is 3.3%, down from a peak of about 8% in June and the lowest since early February.
Global Info Tech saw the largest 2-week % net selling (Oct 5 to Oct 16) on GS's record (10+ years, -3.3 SDs), driven by both long sales and short sales.
Mag 7 net exposure has risen to a new record high. The gap between US Semis and Software net exposures has continued to narrow.

SPCX rose 8% after strong operating results, with revenue growth across all three operating segments. The Super Intelligence segment had the largest dollar momentum, driven by scale in its Cloud Services business.
SPCX management expects Starship launches to accelerate, targeting weekly launches in 1H27 and roughly twice-weekly by the end of 2027 as reusability improves.
SPCX management disclosed that both SPCX and TSLA have formed special committees of independent directors to discuss a potential business combination.
Read-across from the SPCX print: hyperscalers traded lower on increased competition (GOOGL -1%, MSFT -50bps, AMZN flat), while semis rose (SMH +2%).
SMCI rose 12% on a positive pre-announcement guiding net sales well above consensus. DELL rose 5% and HPE rose 4% in sympathy.
